leaders.notes: Became president February 26, 1993; Lamar University was moved into the Texas State University System in 1995 during his tenure. Submitted his resignation in March 1998. Prior and subsequent roles not verified from official sources.
Served as interim president between Rex Cottle and James Simmons. Prior and subsequent roles not verified from official sources.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the College of Fine Arts and Communication and interim executive director of university advancement
leaders.nextRole: Resigned the presidency to return to the Lamar faculty as a music instructor; named President Emeritus
leaders.notes: Took office September 1, 1999 after more than four decades on the Lamar faculty (dean of fine arts, music department chair, director of bands). Resigned effective July 1, 2013; the Texas State University System named him President Emeritus and named the Simmons Music Building for him.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the Michael F. Price College of Business
leaders.notes: Came to Lamar in 2013 after more than six years as dean of the Price College of Business at the University of Oklahoma. Announced retirement effective June 30, 2021, then became the 19th president of Oklahoma City University on July 1, 2021.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Sitting president; 16th president of Lamar University, assumed office July 2021 and formally installed November 2021. Came directly from Marshall University, where he was provost and senior vice president for academic affairs. No active presidential search.

university: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center, New Orleans

leaders.priorTitle: Longtime LSU faculty member and administrator (clinical and administrative roles)
leaders.priorInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans (same institution)
leaders.nextRole: Named Senior Vice President and CEO of the LSU Health Sciences Center in August 2000; died January 3, 2001
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans
leaders.notes: Appointed chancellor December 9, 1994 (in office in 1996). An otolaryngologist recruited to the LSU School of Medicine in 1968. Transitioned to Senior Vice President/CEO of the health sciences center in 2000 and died in January 2001.

leaders.priorTitle: Clinical and administrative faculty (about ten years at the institution)
leaders.priorInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans (same institution)
leaders.nextRole: Later served as Chair of the Louisiana Board of Regents
leaders.notes: Served as interim chancellor between Mervin Trail and John Rock. Had spent roughly a decade at LSUHSC in clinical and administrative capacities. Only female leader in this chain.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Medicine
leaders.priorInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans (same institution)
leaders.nextRole: Senior Vice President for Medical Affairs and Founding Dean of the Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine
leaders.notes: Chancellor and CEO 2002-2005; an obstetrician-gynecologist who had been dean of the LSU medical school. Resigned in 2005 and became founding dean of the medical school at Florida International University.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Medicine (recruited 2004)
leaders.priorInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans (same institution)
leaders.nextRole: Stepped down amid audit findings and remained on the faculty as a vascular surgeon
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans / LCMC Health
leaders.notes: Chancellor from November 2005 to November 2021; had returned to his alma mater as dean of the School of Medicine in 2004. Resigned in October/November 2021 after an LSU audit alleged nepotism and improper spending.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Medicine (2007-2021)
leaders.priorInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans (same institution)
leaders.nextRole: Ousted from the chancellorship in February 2026
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: LSU Health Sciences Center New Orleans
leaders.notes: Joined the medical school faculty in 1984 and was dean of medicine from 2007 to 2021. Appointed interim chancellor in October 2021 when Hollier stepped down, then named permanent chancellor in February 2024. Fired/ousted in February 2026 and replaced by David Guzick.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor of LSU Health Shreveport (resigned 2025); earlier Senior Vice President for Health Affairs and President of UF Health
leaders.priorInstitution: LSU Health Shreveport (formerly University of Florida)
leaders.notes: Sitting head, appointed February 2026 to replace the ousted Steve Nelson. His official title is Senior Vice Chancellor of LSU Health New Orleans (the campus head title, historically Chancellor, was designated Senior Vice Chancellor under a 2026 LSU reorganization). Had been forced to resign as chancellor of LSU Health Shreveport in 2025; leadership at the center is currently in flux.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs (earlier dean of engineering)
leaders.notes: 13th president; selected February 20, 1987 to succeed F. Jay Taylor and took office July 1, 1987 (in office in 1996). A chemical/biomedical engineer who joined Tech in 1967 and became VP for academic affairs in 1980. Retired June 30, 2013 after 26 years, the longest presidential tenure in Tech history.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Research and Development
leaders.notes: 14th president, July 1, 2013 to December 31, 2023. Named Tech's VP for Research and Development in 2004 and helped lead the university's rise to high research activity. Announced retirement in September 2023.

leaders.priorTitle: President and CEO of the University of Louisiana System
leaders.notes: Sitting president; 15th president of Louisiana Tech, took office January 1, 2024. Came directly from serving nearly seven years as president and CEO of the University of Louisiana System (Tech's own system). No active presidential search.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President
leaders.nextRole: President of the University of Tennessee
leaders.notes: 15th president, 1991-1999 (in office in 1996). Had been senior vice president at George Mason University for nearly a decade. Left Marshall July 31, 1999 to become president of the University of Tennessee (served 1999-2001).

leaders.priorTitle: Bank executive and member of the University System of West Virginia Board of Trustees
leaders.priorInstitution: Banking industry (Huntington, WV) / University System of West Virginia Board of Trustees
leaders.nextRole: Returned to business and civic life; died in 2015
leaders.notes: Officially listed as Audy Michael Perry, 16th president (interim). A Huntington businessman and bank executive who agreed to serve about six months after Gilley's departure until Dan Angel took office. Died in 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: President of Stephen F. Austin State University
leaders.notes: 17th president, took office January 1, 2000. Came directly from serving as president of Stephen F. Austin State University (1992-1999). Led an $83 million capital campaign; resigned effective December 31, 2004.

leaders.priorTitle: Trial attorney and member of the Marshall University Board of Governors
leaders.priorInstitution: Marshall University Board of Governors (Farrell, White & Legg law firm, Huntington, WV)
leaders.notes: 18th president (interim). A distinguished trial lawyer and Marshall Board of Governors member who became interim president on January 1, 2005 after Angel resigned, serving until Stephen Kopp took office July 1, 2005.

leaders.priorTitle: Special assistant to the chancellor, Ohio Board of Regents (previously Provost of Ohio University)
leaders.priorInstitution: Ohio Board of Regents (previously Ohio University)
leaders.nextRole: Died in office of a heart attack, December 17, 2014
leaders.notes: 36th president (special-collections 19th), July 1, 2005 until his death December 17, 2014. Had been provost of Ohio University (2002-2004) and then a special assistant to the chancellor at the Ohio Board of Regents.

leaders.priorTitle: Longtime coal and natural-resources CEO and member of the Marshall University Board of Governors
leaders.priorInstitution: Marshall University Board of Governors (coal/natural resource industry)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to business and civic life
leaders.notes: Interim president named December 29, 2014 after Kopp's death, serving until January 2016. A career executive with more than fifty years in the coal and natural-resource industries and a Marshall Board of Governors member.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President
leaders.nextRole: Remained at Marshall as a part-time independent contractor advising incoming president Brad Smith
leaders.notes: 37th president, assumed office January 2016 after nearly six years as provost and executive vice president of Mississippi State University. Agreed to conclude his presidency December 31, 2021 to ease the transition to Brad Smith, then advised Smith part-time through 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Chairman of the Board (former President and CEO)
leaders.notes: Sitting president; 38th president of Marshall, took office January 2022. A Marshall alumnus (Kenova, WV native) who was executive chairman of Intuit after serving as its president and CEO from 2008 to 2018. No active presidential search.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Dean of Arts and Sciences (and Dean of the College of Mathematical and Physical Sciences)
leaders.notes: 20th president, began his term in 1996 (the anchor leader for this institution). A physicist who spent 26 years at Ohio State, ending as executive dean of Arts and Sciences. Retired in 2006 and later wrote 'Saving Alma Mater.'

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences
leaders.notes: 21st president, July 1, 2006 to June 30, 2016. A geographer who spent 31 years at the University of Washington, serving as dean of the College of Arts and Sciences from 1998 to 2006. Announced retirement in May 2015.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President and Associate Provost (and William K. Warren Foundation Dean of the College of Science)
leaders.notes: Sitting president; 22nd president of Miami, took office July 2016. Came from the University of Notre Dame, where he was vice president and associate provost and dean of the College of Science (earlier dean of engineering at Brown University). No active presidential search.
